summary: Hakuju Ui was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Junjirō Takakusu and at the University of Tübingen under Richard von Garbe, later holding professorships at Tokyo, Tohoku, and Komazawa universities.

Halle O'Neal specializes in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and history and archaeology. She earned her PhD from the University of Kansas around 2005–2011, studying under doctoral supervisor Sherry Fowler.

Hammalawa Saddhatissa worked in Buddhist studies and Indology, studying at Sastrodoya and Vidyodaya Pirivenas, BHU, and the University of Edinburgh. He served at BHU, SOAS, the University of Toronto, and headed the London Buddhist Vihara from around 1957 to 1990.
Hank Glassman is a scholar of Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. His academic career includes a faculty affiliation at Haverford College, attested in 2009 and 2019.

Hanns Oertel worked in Indology and linguistics, earning his doctorate at Yale under William Dwight Whitney. He taught at Yale (1891–1917), Marburg (~1920–1925), and held the chair of Indian and Iranian philology at Munich (1925–1935).
Hannu Riikonen studied at the University of Helsinki from around 1967 to 1978. He later served as a professor at the University of Helsinki from circa 1999 to 2016.

Hans Hartog, an Indologist and linguist, studied at Tübingen, Kirchliche Hochschule Bethel, and Munich. He completed his PhD at Marburg (1937–1939) under Friedrich Heiler, also studying under Hanns Oertel, Walther Wüst, and others.

Hans Henrich Hock is a linguist and Indologist who studied at Yale University from around 1965 to 1971. He served as Professor of Linguistics and Sanskrit at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign from circa 1967 to 2013.

Hans T. Bakker is an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied under Jacob Ensink. He held posts at the University of Groningen from 1978 to 1995 and later served as a curator at the British Museum.
Hans-Werner Köhler was an Indologist. He studied under Eduard Hermann and completed doctoral work under Ernst Waldschmidt (attested 1973).
Hanung Kim works in Tibetology and history and archaeology. Kim earned a master's degree from Columbia University and a PhD from Harvard University under doctoral supervisor Leonard van der Kuijp.

Hara Prasad Sastri was a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He served as Principal of Sanskrit College and University (attested 1905) and Joint Philological Secretary at the Asiatic Society (attested 1905–1911).

Harald Hauptmann specialized in history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. After studying at Heidelberg University, he held posts there (~1974–2001), the German Archaeological Institute at Istanbul (~1994–2001), and the Heidelberg Academy of Sciences and Humanities (~1989–2018).

Haraprasad Shastri was a scholar in Indology, history and archaeology, and Buddhist studies. Educated at Sanskrit College and Presidency University, Kolkata, he held posts at Hare School, Presidency University, Sanskrit College (~1900–1908), and the University of Dhaka (~1921–1924).

Hari Damodar Velankar was an Indologist who studied under H. M. Bhadkamkar. His career included posts at Wilson College, Mumbai (attested 1944) and as Joint Director at Bharatiya Vidya Bhavan (attested 1959–1960).
Hari Shankar Prasad is a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied at Banaras Hindu University, as well as under Ramakant Tripathi and doctoral supervisor Jan Willem de Jong.

Haridas Bhattacharyya was a scholar of philosophy and Indology who studied at Scottish Church College and the University of Calcutta. He held academic posts at Calcutta (~1915–1921), the University of Dhaka (~1921–1947), and Banaras Hindu University (~1947–1956).
Haridas Sinharay was an Indologist. He held an academic post at Maulana Azad College, attested in 1970 and 1990.
Harivallabh Bhayani was a scholar of Indology and linguistics who studied at Samaldas Arts College and Bharatiya Vidya Bhavan. He later served as Director of the L.D. Institute of Indology.

Harjot Oberoi specializes in religious studies and history and archaeology. He studied at the Australian National University from around 1980 to 1987 and held a post at the University of British Columbia starting circa 1987.
